selected.title: Webb spots a rare ring-shaped galaxy from the early universe
selected.summary: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope identified a rare ring galaxy dating to roughly two billion years after the Big Bang, with a likely colliding galaxy nearby.
selected.why_it_matters: The unexpected shape offers a glimpse of how collisions can reshape galaxies, including in the universe’s early eras.
selected.challenge_question: What may have helped give this early galaxy its ring shape?
selected.answer_explanation: Researchers interpret the nearby galaxy as a possible intruder whose collision may have produced the ring. That explanation is supported by the observations, but remains an interpretation.
selected.butterfly_question: How can a cosmic collision turn a galaxy into a ring?
